correctness.rationale: The greedy earliest embedding of each deletion output partitions the two skipped positions; the four cases combine using the three-letter identity u_i(1−u_{i+1})+u_{i+1}(1−j_i)=1−j_i to give B=binom(K,2)+n−1−J. Under independent uniform q-ary letters, the adjacent-inequality variables and the distance-two equality variables each form independent Bernoulli families because their constraint edges are forests. Only neighboring u_i u_(i+1) and j_i have nonzero quadratic covariance p/q², giving the exact mean and variance. Write Z=n−1−K, H=binom(n,2)−B=nZ−Z(Z+3)/2+J. Mixed factorial moments for Z,J converge to independent Poisson(θ) because all overlapping edge patterns have vanishing weight when q~n. Continuous mapping gives the two-scale joint limit. H=0 iff Z=J=0 for n>=3, and counting words with both distances unequal gives the exact max probability.
